rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 5 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008): the prototype wins by default, and claim 6 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010): a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides how it does it. The prototype is not self-contradictory: it saves and shows the template's transporter country, and its review works the country out from the approval number's prefix (prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-102), so seeding the approval number already brings the country back. The real frontend stores the transporter's country as an answer (repo-frontend-p12-090), and a private transporter has no approval number to work it out from, so the only way the real service can show the prototype's outcome is to carry the saved country across.
outcome: Using a template seeds the transporter's country along with its name, address, approval number and type. The prototype's design saves and shows the country and, after a template is used, shows the same country again (worked out from the seeded approval number); the real service stores the country as an answer and has no approval number for a private transporter, so it carries the saved country into the new notification to give the same result.
